newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - February 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - February 4.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.
- Serious difficulties have arisen in relation to the levels and extent of emergency cover to be provided in Dublin's major acute hospitals if next Moday's strike by nurses goes ahead.
- Hopes of averting serious industrial action by Aer Lingus cabin crew from midnight on Wednesday have risen, following an invitation to talks at the Labour Relations Commission.
- The contents of Judge Gerard Buchanan's report into payments to politicians by Dunnes Stores are expected to become public today.
- Ireland's President Mary Robinson said on Monday she travels to Northern Ireland "in friendship" and would "regret" if her visits were misunderstood.
- Irish Life has suspended 100 employees and expects to suspend more of its sales staff today as the dispute over the new sales structures and practices accelerates.
- Ireland's prison chiefs have revealed for the first time the true extent of jail overcrowding.
- Smuggled cigarettes being sold on the streets of Dublin and other EU cities are at the centre of a 10 billion Irish pound loss to European taxpayers, a report reveals today.

- Ireland's Electricity Supply Board has promised to pay cash to domestic and business users if the company fails to meet 12 guarantees in a new customer charter announced on Monday by Energy Minister Alan Dukes.
- Six workers at the Sellafield nuclear plant were contaminated after radioactive material leaked into the building on Monday.
- The state has demanded a breakdown of a 3 million Irish pound legal bill from a firm of solicitors which represented the Goodman group at the Beef Tribunal.

- The unions which represent Ireland's 26,000 nurses are pressing ahead with plans for next Monday's strike as Labour Court "exploratory" moves open today in a desperate bid to avert the first-ever nationwide industrial action by nurses.
- Ireland's Mountjoy prison authorities admitted on Monday it would be impossible to stop the flow of drugs reaching prisoners.
- Ireland's prospects of joining EMU on day one have seriously been undermined by views expressed by top German officials in the past few days.
